advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Route the discovery-phase Terraform parse (build_snapshot's _child_dirs/_reverse_caller_dirs) through run_in_worker like query-time parsing, or document/justify why in-process discovery parsing is acceptable despite the worker-isolation invariant.
evidence: terraform_index.py:129-133 `_child_dirs` -> `from . import terraform_parse as tp` and `_safe_parse(root, rel_file, tp)`
terraform_index.py:181 `_safe_parse` calls `return tp.parse_document(text)` directly (no worker)

terraform_parse.py:4-9 docstring: `parse_document ... the single module-level callable the grounding worker boundary ... invokes in a spawn subprocess — so a hang/segfault in the C-ish parser becomes a fail-open abstain, never a host crash`
terraform_tools.py open_session calls `tfi.build_snapshot(str(root), selected)` synchronously in the parent process, which triggers _closure -> _child_dirs/_reverse_caller_dirs parsing
advisory.finding: terraform_index closure-building (_child_dirs, _reverse_caller_dirs via _safe_parse) calls terraform_parse.parse_document DIRECTLY in-process during build_snapshot (invoked from open_session in the parent), running the hcl2/lark parser OUTSIDE the run_in_worker subprocess boundary. This contradicts the documented invariant that hcl2 is only touched inside the worker so a parser hang/segfault degrades to a fail-open abstention.
scenarios: A malformed or adversarial .tf file in the module closure that hangs or segfaults the hcl2/lark parser during snapshot build
Closure discovery over a repo with many/large .tf files

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Contain discovery-time parse failures (hang/segfault) via the worker boundary rather than a Python-level try/except that cannot see signal deaths or hangs.
evidence: terraform_index.py:182 `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — discovery is best-effort; a bad file is skipped`
harness.py:279-281 documents that a worker dying on a signal (SIGSEGV/SIGABRT from a bad C parse) is only survivable via the worker boundary, not an in-process try/except
advisory.finding: _safe_parse's `except Exception` guard is described as making discovery best-effort, but it cannot catch a C-extension segfault, an OS-level abort, or an infinite hang in the lark/hcl2 parser — the very failure modes the worker boundary exists to contain. Discovery-time parse thus has no timeout or crash containment.
scenarios: A .tf file that triggers a lark segfault or non-terminating parse encountered during closure discovery

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Reconcile the distribution name between _capabilities.py install_hint (`nava-rebar`) and docs/grounding.md (`rebar`) so both cite the actual PyPI package.
evidence: _capabilities.py: `install_hint="pip install 'nava-rebar[grounding-terraform]'"`
docs/grounding.md: `pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'   # or: uv sync --extra grounding-terraform`
advisory.finding: The capability `install_hint` names the package `nava-rebar[grounding-terraform]` while docs/grounding.md instructs `pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'`. This provenance/naming inconsistency can send operators to the wrong (possibly unclaimed/typosquattable) package name.
scenarios: An operator copies the docs name `rebar` instead of the published distribution name
A different name resolves to an unrelated or malicious package on PyPI

evidence: `idx = counters.get(btype, 0); counters[btype] = idx + 1`
`entries = data.get(btype); ... entry = entries[idx]`
spans come from a separate tree walk in `_block_spans` while entries come from `hcl2.loads(text)` — the two orderings are assumed identical but never cross-checked
advisory.finding: `_declarations` correlates `hcl2.loads()` list entries with `_block_spans()` tree blocks positionally by a per-block-type counter, assuming loads() preserves one list entry per block in document order. If hcl2.loads merges multiple same-type/same-label blocks or reorders them (e.g. two `resource` blocks of differing types, or a block loads() collapses), the span index (`entries[idx]`) silently binds a declaration to the WRONG source span, so a `refuted` receipt/evidence would carry a misattributed line range.

evidence: Shared resource: one dict created at src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:202 `tf_usage_sink: dict[str, Any] = {}` and bound into the Pass-1 hook at line 204-206 `tf_pass1_hook = terraform_seam.pass1_tool_hook(repo_root=tf_code_root, usage_sink=tf_usage_sink)`.

≥2 concurrent executors: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/pass1.py:434-436 `with ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=max_workers) as ex:` … `ag_futs = [_submit_ctx(ex, _chunk, [c], True) for c in agent]` — one worker thread per agentic T10 criterion; the same tf_provider is threaded verbatim into every _chunk (pass1.py:351).

READ + WRITE window: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/terraform_seam.py:266-273 `fetches = usage_sink.get("distinct_fetches")` … `usage_sink["distinct_fetches"] = merge_synthetic_reads(fetches, …)`; merge_synthetic_reads returns a NEW list (src/rebar/llm/usage_log.py:286 `merged = list(distinct_fetches)`), so it is a non-atomic read-modify-write, not an in-place append.

Finalizer runs on the worker thread: src/rebar/llm/plan_review/passes.py:334-338 `try: result = runner.run(req) finally: if tf_finalize is not None: tf_finalize()` — each concurrent _chunk thread invokes _fold_usage.

Sibling/absence: no lock guards the sink — search of terraform_seam.py and passes.py for `Lock` returns (no matches); _fold_usage's docstring claims it is 'deterministic and idempotent-per-target' but that only covers ORDER, not concurrent interleaving of the get/set pair.

Harm: lost update — thread A reads the base list, thread B reads the same base list, both write back their own merged copy; the last write wins and the other thread's concrete_reads/membership_globs are dropped from `distinct_fetches`, which is the SIGNED read-set / attestation currency material (usage_log.py:264-266), corrupting the read-set digest — not merely a logged metric.
advisory.finding: Concurrent Pass-1 agentic T10 chunks fold their Terraform grounding reads into a single shared `tf_usage_sink['distinct_fetches']` via an unlocked read-modify-write, so simultaneous finalizers lose one another's synthetic reads from the signed read-set.
advisory.suggested_fix: Serialize the fold: hold a threading.Lock around the get/merge/set in _fold_usage (create the lock alongside tf_usage_sink and pass it through the hook), OR have each session finalize into its own list and merge all per-session lists into tf_usage_sink once on the main thread after the ThreadPoolExecutor in run_pass1 has joined.

evidence: `_targets` returns `sorted(self._snapshot.modules)` when module_dir is empty (terraform_tools.py:238-240)
`_find_declaration` appends a match for every module_dir that contains the address (terraform_tools.py:223-231)
`if len(matches) > 1: return self._abstain(... "duplicate_address" ...)` (terraform_tools.py:162-165)
advisory.finding: When `lookup_declaration` is called with an empty `module_path`, `_targets` returns ALL snapshot modules and `_find_declaration` aggregates matches across every module; a declaration that exists (e.g. `variable.region`) in two independent modules yields `len(matches) > 1` and abstains with `duplicate_address` instead of refuting the asserted absence. The same name legitimately existing in separate modules is not a genuine ambiguity for an absence-refutation.

evidence: `_tf_files_in_dir`: `for name in os.listdir(base): if not _has_tf_suffix(name, _TF_SUFFIXES): continue; if not (base / name).is_file(): continue` — `.is_file()` follows symlinks and there is no realpath-containment check on the file (terraform_index.py:117-123)
`_real_contained` is only invoked from `_resolve_child_dir` for DIRECTORIES (terraform_index.py:157), never for the individual files returned by `_tf_files_in_dir`
`_parse_file` reads the admitted path directly: `data = (self._root / rel_file).read_bytes()` with no symlink/containment guard (terraform_tools.py:277)
ADR 0111 asserts the guard: 'rejects escaping symlinks' / 'an escaping symlink is refused (path_outside_snapshot)' — but that guarantee is enforced only at dir granularity
advisory.finding: Per-file symlink escape is not guarded: `.tf`/`.tf.json` files enumerated inside a contained module directory are filtered only by suffix and `(base/name).is_file()` (which follows symlinks), so a `.tf` file that is a symlink to an out-of-repo target (e.g. `infra/x.tf -> ../../secrets/prod.tf`) is admitted to the snapshot and read via `read_bytes()` with no per-file real-path containment check. Directory-level containment (`_real_contained`) does not cover the leaf files.
advisory.suggested_fix: In `_tf_files_in_dir`, after the `.is_file()` check, drop any entry whose `os.path.realpath(base / name)` does not stay within `os.path.realpath(root)` (reuse `_real_contained`), matching the escaping-symlink guarantee ADR 0111 documents.

evidence: _capabilities.py: install_hint="pip install 'nava-rebar[grounding-terraform]'"
docs/grounding.md: "pip install 'rebar[grounding-terraform]'   # or: uv sync --extra grounding-terraform"
advisory.finding: The install hint for the new extra is inconsistent between manifest/capability metadata and docs: `_capabilities.py` uses package name `nava-rebar` while `docs/grounding.md` uses `rebar`.

evidence: `_module_call`: `for call in facts.get("module_calls", []): if call.get("name") == name: return call` (terraform_tools.py:388-392) — returns first, no duplicate detection
contrast: declaration lookup abstains on `duplicate_address` when `len(matches) > 1`
advisory.finding: `_module_call` returns the FIRST module call whose name matches, ignoring the possibility of duplicate `module "x"` blocks. Unlike declaration lookup (which detects duplicates), a duplicated module name silently resolves against the first source, so `resolve_reference` on `module.x.out` can refute against the wrong child module.

evidence: `self._finalized = True` is set but never checked in `lookup_declaration`/`resolve_reference`/`_parse_file` (terraform_tools.py:145)
`finalize` clears `_concrete_reads`/`_membership`; a later query re-populates them but they will not be folded again unless finalize is re-called
advisory.finding: `finalize()` is not idempotent-safe against double invocation feeding `_fold_usage`: it returns the accumulated Usage then clears the ledger, but sets `_finalized=True` without guarding subsequent queries or a second finalize. A second `finalize()` returns an empty Usage and further queries after finalize still run against a cleared cache/ledger silently, so post-finalize reads are lost from the signed read-set.

evidence: `_safe_parse`: `except Exception:  # noqa: BLE001 — discovery is best-effort; a bad file is skipped` returns `{}` (terraform_index.py)
`_child_dirs`/`_reverse_caller_dirs` iterate `parsed.get("module_calls", [])` — an empty dict yields no calls, identical to a truly call-free file
closure silently omits modules that fail discovery-parse, so a module reachable only through an unparseable caller is invisible to the snapshot
advisory.finding: `_reverse_caller_dirs` and `_child_dirs` swallow every parse failure via `_safe_parse` (bare `except Exception: return {}`), so a module whose `.tf` fails to parse is silently dropped from the whole-module closure. Reverse-caller/child discovery then produces the same empty result whether a file genuinely declares no module calls or the parser never succeeded — a fail-open check whose negative outcome is indistinguishable from the check never running.

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Declare `lark` as an explicit pinned dependency in the `grounding-terraform` extra since terraform_parse.py imports it directly.
evidence: `import hcl2  # lazy: keeps \`import rebar\` lean (lean-import oracle)` followed by `import lark`
pyproject.toml extra declares only `grounding-terraform = ["python-hcl2==8.1.3"]` with no `lark` pin
The code depends on `lark.Tree`/`Tree.meta` span shape which the pyproject comment itself calls 'version-sensitive', yet lark's version is unconstrained
dropped.finding: terraform_parse.py directly imports `lark` (`import lark`, and uses `lark.Tree`) but `lark` is not declared as a direct dependency in the `grounding-terraform` extra — it is only present transitively via `python-hcl2`. A direct import of an undeclared (transitive) dependency means a future python-hcl2 release that changes or drops its `lark` backend would silently break this code with no version constraint protecting it.
scenarios: python-hcl2 bumps or replaces its lark backend in a patch release picked up on a lock refresh, changing Tree.meta span semantics
A downstream install resolves a different lark version than tested
dropped.suggested_fix: Add an explicit `lark==<tested version>` (or a tight range) alongside `python-hcl2==8.1.3` in the `grounding-terraform` extra, since the code imports `lark` directly and relies on version-sensitive `Tree.meta` span behavior.
